enamor

/ih-NAM-er/ - rhymes with hammer · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Enamor means to fill with love or fascination.

One week at her grandmother's forge was enough to enamor Lena of blacksmithing for life.

Example

The planetarium's creaky star projector enamored generations of schoolchildren; ushers joked that half the city's astronomers could date their careers to one field trip under its painted dome.

Enamor means to fill with love or lasting fascination, and it usually appears in the passive: you are enamored of — or with — something. It is stronger than 'like' and warmer than 'impress': what enamors you pulls you back again and again.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

bewitch: Bewitch means to fascinate so completely that it feels like a spell — stronger and stranger than enamor. Being enamored is warm, human affection that keeps drawing you back; being bewitched hints that your judgment has been taken over by something you cannot resist.

captivate: Captivate means to seize delighted attention and hold it — a captivating speaker owns the room for as long as she talks. Enamor goes deeper and lasts longer: it plants real affection, so the pull is still there long after the performance has ended.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

repel: to drive interest away entirely

disenchant: to break the spell and let the fondness drain out

Where it sits · how deep and lasting the delight

please → charm → enamor

please vs. enamor: Please is the faintest glow — a pleased visitor nods and moves on; it stops far short of enamor.

charm vs. enamor: Charm goes further than please but stops short of enamor: a charmed guest smiles all evening; an enamored one is still talking about it in June.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — en-: in; cause to be

Root — amor: love - Latin amor

Put it together: En- (cause to be in) + amor (love) = to put someone into love. A textbook case of this unit's prefix: Old French enamourer built the verb exactly as it looks, and English kept the pattern — which is why the word so often appears as enamored of: love you have been placed inside.

Use the root in a new word: amateur: An amateur astronomer in Ohio spotted the comet two nights before the big observatories did.

Root Check

Word Choice

warm / literary

Enamor is a touch bookish and almost always passive: enamored of a city, enamored with a craft. For quick attraction, charmed or taken with is lighter. Its unit-mate enthrall grips the attention; enamor claims the heart — an enthralled visitor cannot look away, while an enamored one comes back the next day in love. And nobody is enamored of a tax form; keep it for real affection.
